title_en: Jiangning County Dongshan Town Subsidiary Company v. Jiangsu Province Nanjing Airport Expressway Management Office — appeal concerning dispute over compensation for damages

full_text_en:
Jiangning County Dongshan Town Subsidiary Company v. Jiangsu Nanjing Airport Expressway Administrative Office — appeal case concerning a dispute over compensation for damages

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Jiangsu Nanjing Airport Expressway Administrative Office.
Legal representative: Jiang Lei, Director.
Agents ad litem: Zhou Yuanbo, Zhang Xiaoling, lawyers of Nanjing Zhongshan Law Firm.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance): Jiangsu Province Jiangning County Dongshan Town Subsidiary Company.
Legal representative: Tian Shusheng, Manager.
Agents ad litem: Li Min, Zhu Honglan, lawyers of Nanjing Yonghe Law Firm.

The appellant, Jiangsu Nanjing Airport Expressway Administrative Office (hereinafter referred to as the Expressway Administrative Office), dissatisfied with the first instance civil judgment rendered by the Yuhuatai District People's Court of Nanjing in the case concerning a dispute over compensation for damages with the appellee, Jiangsu Province Jiangning County Dongshan Town Subsidiary Company (hereinafter referred to as the Subsidiary Company), filed an appeal with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court.

The Nanjing Intermediate People’s Court, upon trial, found the following facts:

At 19:10 hours on November 20, 1997, Sun Jiafu, a driver of the appellee Subsidiary Company, was driving a Santana sedan with license plate number Su L10789 southward along the Nanjing Airport Expressway. When the vehicle reached the location at 19K+200M, the driver suddenly discovered a piece of waterproof canvas measuring 2×1.2 meters that had fallen from a preceding vehicle on the road ahead. Unable to avoid it in time, the vehicle collided with the road’s eastern guardrail, resulting in deformation of the vehicle body, engine damage, tire detachment, and destruction of the trunk’s steel rim. Inside the vehicle, Tian Shusheng, seated in the front passenger seat, suffered a laceration to the back of his head; the three persons seated in the rear were thrown out of the vehicle and injured. Among them, Pan Xinghua died despite rescue efforts on the following day; Wen Sicheng was assessed by forensic medical examination conducted by the Nanjing Public Security Bureau as having a thoracic injury classified as Grade 9 disability and a head and facial injury classified as Grade 10 disability; Wang Jianying had multiple lumps on her head. The Expressway Highway Brigade of the Nanjing Public Security Bureau Traffic Police Detachment issued a Road Traffic Accident Liability Determination on December 12, 1997, concluding: The driver Sun Jiafu was driving normally on the expressway and could not have foreseen the obstacle on the road ahead, and committed no traffic violation at the time of the accident; the passengers Pan Xinghua, Wen Sicheng, Wang Jianying, and Tian Shusheng committed no traffic violation at the time of the accident; this accident was an unforeseeable accident. Through mediation, the Subsidiary Company, as the vehicle owner, entered into a road traffic accident damage compensation agreement with the victims of this accident: the Subsidiary Company was to pay Pan Xinghua's relatives rescue expenses, funeral expenses, death compensation, and dependent living expenses totaling RMB 91,242; to pay the injured Wen Sicheng medical expenses, lost work income, nutritional expenses, nursing expenses, living allowance for the disabled, and transportation expenses totaling RMB 47,328; to pay the injured Tian Shusheng medical expenses and lost work income totaling RMB 5,388.30; to pay the injured Wang Jianying medical expenses and lost work income totaling RMB 1,340; and the Subsidiary Company bore vehicle damage costs, guardrail damage costs, accident rescue costs, and accident handling costs totaling RMB 30,620. The total of the above amounts was RMB 175,918.30. The Subsidiary Company incurred a total of RMB 231,129.25 in expenses for handling this accident, and subsequently recovered RMB 33,260 from China Ping An Insurance Company under a vehicle damage insurance claim. In October 1998, the Subsidiary Company filed a lawsuit with the Yuhuatai District People's Court of Nanjing against the appellant Expressway Administrative Office, claiming that the Expressway Administrative Office, having collected vehicle tolls, failed to perform its duty of ensuring road safety and unimpeded traffic, thereby causing the Subsidiary Company to suffer substantial property losses, and sought compensation of RMB 231,129.25.

It was further found: The appellant Expressway Administrative Office is a legal person of a public institution under ownership by the whole people. The duties or scope of services registered on its legal person registration certificate for public institutions include road administration, highway maintenance, statutory fee collection, and operational development. Its funding source is self-financing. Authorized by the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Communications, the Expressway Administrative Office exercises the powers of road administration and statutory fee collection. Pursuant to such authorization, the Expressway Administrative Office may collect vehicle tolls from vehicles passing through the Nanjing Airport Expressway, carry out road administration, and impose administrative penalties on entities or individuals that violate road administration and vehicle toll collection regulations.

The court of first instance, upon trial, held: Because of the toll collection, a contractual relationship for the paid use of the highway was formed between the Expressway Administrative Office and the Subsidiary Company. The Expressway Administrative Office should have ensured that vehicles belonging to the Subsidiary Company could use the expressway safely and smoothly. The road obstacle that caused the accident to the Subsidiary Company's vehicle, which had been driving normally, should have been discovered and removed by the Expressway Administrative Office in a timely manner. The Expressway Administrative Office's failure to discover and remove the obstacle due to negligence in patrol constituted a failure to perform its duties and contractual obligations. The Expressway Administrative Office should bear liability for compensating the direct economic losses suffered by the Subsidiary Company as a result of this accident. Accordingly, the court rendered judgment: the Expressway Administrative Office shall compensate the Subsidiary Company for losses in the amount of RMB 142,658.30; the case acceptance fee of RMB 4,360 shall be borne by the Expressway Administrative Office.

The appellant, the Expressway Administrative Office, alleged on appeal: First, the appellant's collection of vehicle tolls from the appellee was an act of administrative management, which could only create an administrative relationship between the parties, not a contractual relationship. The first instance judgment's handling of this case based on contractual relations was an improper application of law. Second, the first instance finding that the appellant was negligent in patrol was unsupported by evidence. Third, the road traffic accident liability determination issued by the traffic police department did not indicate that the appellant was at fault for this accident; therefore, the appellant should not be held liable for this accident. Fourth, the appellee should have sued the party responsible for discarding the canvas, but instead sued the appellant, which has no legal basis. The court should have dismissed the appellee's claims but failed to do so, constituting a misjudgment.

The appellee, the Subsidiary Company, did not submit a written response.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held:

The appellant, the Expressway Administrative Office, as a legal person of a public institution, by virtue of the authorization from the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Communications and the scope approved by the registration certificate of the public institution legal person, not only enjoys the administrative power to exercise road administration and collect statutory fees on the Nanjing Airport Expressway on behalf of the authorizing entity, but also has the right to collect vehicle tolls from passing vehicles to fund its operational activities. In accordance with the principle that rights and obligations are consistent, the Expressway Administrative Office, while enjoying the above rights, has the duty to maintain the highway in good condition, safety, and unimpeded condition pursuant to Article 43 of the Highway Law of the People's Republic of China. After the appellee, the Subsidiary Company, fulfilled its obligation to pay vehicle tolls, it acquired the right to use the expressway and to pass safely. Between the Expressway Administrative Office and the Subsidiary Company, due to the act of paying fees, a civil contractual relationship for the paid use of the expressway was formed. Pursuant to Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, civil activities shall adhere to the principles of fairness and equal compensation for value. The Expressway Administrative Office's failure to promptly remove obstacles on the road after collecting tolls, resulting in an accident to the Subsidiary Company's vehicle while passing, constitutes both a tortious act of omission and a breach of contract for failing to perform its duty to ensure highway safety and unimpeded traffic. The first instance judgment's treatment of the matter as a breach of contractual obligations was not improper. The Subsidiary Company's claim for compensation from the Expressway Administrative Office for the losses caused to it by this accident complies with Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China; the Expressway Administrative Office shall bear civil liability for its breach of contract. The first instance court's judgment ordering the Expressway Administrative Office to compensate the Subsidiary Company for losses was correct.

The appellant, the Expressway Administrative Office, is not itself an administrative organ and does not have administrative enforcement powers. The road administration, statutory fee collection, and administrative penalty powers it exercises on behalf of the authorizing entity must be carried out in the name of the authorizing organ, the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Communications. Any administrative acts performed by the Expressway Administrative Office on behalf of the authorizing entity can only create an administrative relationship between the person subject to administration and the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Communications, not between that person and the Expressway Administrative Office. The Expressway Administrative Office may carry out daily operational management of the expressway in its own name. Its collection of tolls from passing vehicles based on its operation and management of the expressway can only create a civil rights-obligations relationship with the toll payer, not an administrative management relationship. Moreover, the State Planning Commission, in its Reply on Issues Concerning the Collection of Vehicle Tolls for Highways, Bridges, and Tunnels (Document No. Ji Ji Guan [1997] 2070) dated October 31, 1997, clearly stated that vehicle tolls are operating fees, not administrative or institutional fees. The appellee, the Subsidiary Company, brought its lawsuit seeking compensation on the ground that the Expressway Administrative Office, after collecting tolls, failed to perform its duties, thereby causing losses, not because it disputed some administrative act performed by the Expressway Administrative Office and therefore sued the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Communications. This case is clearly a civil dispute. The appellant's ground of appeal that "collecting vehicle tolls is an act of administrative management and can only create an administrative relationship between the parties, not a contractual relationship" cannot be sustained.

Maintaining the highway, patrolling the highway, and clearing road obstacles are duties and obligations that the appellant, the Expressway Administrative Office, should perform. Given the modern conditions of the Nanjing Airport Expressway, it is sufficient to ensure that the Expressway Administrative Office can promptly discover and clear any abnormal conditions on the road surface. The Nanjing Airport Expressway has heavy traffic flow and high speeds. In such an environment, the Expressway Administrative Office can only ensure safe passage by conducting diligent and careful patrols. Although the Expressway Administrative Office presented evidence that it had performed patrol duties in accordance with the road administration system, such evidence cannot prove that it had achieved the purpose of ensuring safe passage on the highway. The occurrence of this accident is sufficient to prove that the Expressway Administrative Office was negligent in its patrol. The appellant's ground of appeal that "the first instance finding that the appellant was negligent in patrol is unsupported by evidence" cannot be sustained.

The traffic police's determination concerning this accident only addressed the issue of whether the appellee, the Subsidiary Company, and its passengers had committed any traffic violations or were at fault in this accident; it did not involve the cause or liability of the Expressway Administrative Office. The appellant's ground of appeal that "the road traffic accident liability determination issued by the traffic police department did not indicate that the appellant was at fault for this accident, and therefore the appellant should not be held liable for this accident" cannot be sustained. The road traffic accident liability determination cannot serve as a basis for exonerating the Expressway Administrative Office's liability.

Both parties do not dispute that the waterproof canvas that became a road obstacle was dropped by a third party. As for the civil liability that the third party should bear for the traffic accident losses caused by the dropped canvas, such liability can only be addressed after the Expressway Administrative Office has identified the third party. Under circumstances where the third party has not been identified, the Subsidiary Company, in accordance with the principle of privity of contract, filed suit against the Expressway Administrative Office, claiming that the Expressway Administrative Office, having failed to fulfill its duty to maintain the highway in good condition, safe, and unimpeded condition, should pay compensation in the first instance. Such a claim is lawful. After the Expressway Administrative Office pays compensation in the first instance, it has the right to seek recovery from the third party. Under circumstances where the third party has not been identified, the appellant's ground of appeal that "the appellee should have sued the party responsible for discarding the canvas, but instead sued the appellant, which has no legal basis" cannot be sustained.

In conclusion, the first instance judgment found clear facts, provided sufficient and reliable evidence, correctly applied the law, and rendered an appropriate decision, which should be affirmed. None of the grounds of appeal raised by the Expressway Administrative Office can be sustained and are not adopted. Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, on August 24, 1999, rendered judgment:

Appeal dismissed; the judgment of first instance is affirmed.

The second instance litigation fee of RMB 4,360 shall be borne by the Expressway Administrative Office.
